analysis:
## The Broadcom misread

[Broadcom's stock fell 14%](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-june-10-2026) today after leaving its 2027 AI revenue forecast unchanged — the market treated that as a guide-down. The ripple dragged the entire AI-chip complex, including NVDA. But there is a critical distinction: **Broadcom serves the custom-silicon segment** — Google's TPUs, Amazon's Trainium, hyperscalers building their own AI processors. NVIDIA's business is the **merchant GPU accelerator market**, which serves the same hyperscalers and every other enterprise buying AI compute. These are different stories.

Broadcom saying its custom-chip sales won't accelerate in 2027 tells you that the hyperscalers' *in-house* build programs have plateaued. It says nothing about whether they are still buying NVDA's Blackwell and Rubin — and all evidence says they are, in volume.

## Why $200 matters

The June 8 dossier flagged $200 as the add zone. Today's intraday low was **$199.41** — a textbook test of that level. The close at **~$201.30** confirms it held. With short interest at just 1% of float, this is not a squeeze setup; it is patient accumulation by long-only desks that tracked the level.

The options market agrees: [P/C ratio at 0.78](https://optioncharts.io/options/NVDA), call-heavy flow, and July $215–$225 upside calls being bought. The IV at 42% is elevated but easing off the recent 50% peak — the risk premium is coming out, which is constructive.

## The one real risk

The only thesis-level risk is **FOMC on June 17**. If Warsh signals a rate hike, high-multiple tech (30x forward NVDA at the top of the list) faces another compression leg. A close below $195 on a hike signal would change the call to HOLD and wait for the base. Until June 17, the add zone and the unchanged fundamentals say: BUY the dip.
